correctness.rationale: For every d>=3 and 1<=a<=c, the center is the unique degree-d vertex and the first refinement separates center, internal degree-2 vertices and leaves; subsequent color at round r is exactly the truncated rooted neighborhood type, encoded for leaves by (leaf,min(L,r)) and for internal arm position x by (internal,min(x,r),min(L-x,r)). The arm-to-center and arm-to-leaf distances are distinguished by endpoint degree and potential differences beyond the center are too deep to break an asserted descriptor equality early. If c=a, each arm has unresolved internal middle interval r<=x<=a-r, size <=1 precisely for r>=ceil(a/2). If c>a, short and long leaf colors first separate at r=a+1, and the long internal middle ceases to collide by ceil(c/2); these two necessary conditions suffice for stable orbit classes, giving max(a+1,ceil(c/2)). Independent direct 1-WL implementation tested all d in {3,4,7}, 1<=a<=13, a<=c<=41 (1,365 parameters) without discrepancy, plus code inspection of pinned verifier; this corroborates infinite proof.
